scope: all same-name variants in corrected UI/item/template intersection
primary_review: Sol directly reviewed fixed Git objects, all tier overrides, actual template bindings, execution-chain applicability and the current player examples.

reviewed_conclusions: All 130 fixed-scope file hashes match disk; all 15 own formal pages, 9 implementations, 18 actual bindings, RAW/UI/image evidence and related associations are included.

Eight ordinary weapon variants use stamina-deficit step .20 and five-step cap with per-step tier p=.05/.06/.07/.08; Ogryn Hammer Krourk Mk IIa uses .125 and p=.03/.04/.05/.06, still capped at five steps. At stamina fraction .375, hammer deficit .625 reaches exactly five steps, not more.

Each own full conditional melee-power table replaces the base global .1 fallback through tier override selection; it is not an additive hidden bonus. The ordinary base stepped count is physically one with offset -1, yielding zero at full stamina; the blessing has no hit-driven stacks, timer or cooldown.

The power bonus reads the current stamina fraction and becomes available through Buff/stat-cache updates while the item is held. A stamina change between cache updates is not promised to affect the same action. True unequip removes the source Buff.

All 18 actual Mark action tables are represented: ordinary/heavy/charged/special and push-follow Sweep attacks use melee power; pure push is a push attack; Powermaul P3 chain arc and special push-follow shout use their own non-melee routes; Shield special block/shout is not a melee Sweep. No projectile/shot hit route is claimed.

Examples are correct: at f=.59, deficit .41 with .20 steps gives k=2 and IV power modifier 2*.08=.16; at f=.375 on Krourk with .125 steps gives k=5 and IV .30. The prose explicitly distinguishes power input from final HP damage, impact or cleave results.

The fixed RAW English/Traditional Chinese strings share the recorded localization resource hash; each implementation’s formatter reconstructs the displayed maxima. RAW omits quantization and attack-type details, which are correctly treated as uncovered; no false mistranslation claim is made.
